title: Evo 2 designs whole phage genomes that kill E. coli
friendlyTitle: AI designed viruses that killed harmful bacteria in the lab
summary: Stanford researchers used the Evo 2 genome model to design nearly 300 bacteriophages, then found 16 strong E. coli killers in laboratory tests. A cocktail of the generated phages also overcame bacteria resistant to the original natural phage.
friendlySummary: Stanford scientists used AI to design tiny viruses called phages. Sixteen of them were very good at killing E. coli bacteria in tests.
whyItMatters: This is a concrete laboratory result, not just a computer prediction, and it points toward new ways to tackle antibiotic resistance. It also raises the stakes for biosecurity controls around models that can write functional genomes.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This could help create new treatments when antibiotics stop working. It also shows why powerful biology AI needs strong safety checks.
